procedures.name: Device Record Capture
procedures.applies_when: When a new device is provisioned or an existing device record is updated.

inputs.source: Device Inventory file / column "last eSIM transfer date"

steps: Record device type (phone, tablet, router, watch, other) in the Device Management System using the Device Record template (CSV format).
Record model in the Device Management System using the Device Record template (CSV format).
If an IMEI number is provided, record it; otherwise leave the field blank (IMEI number is optional) in the Device Record template (CSV format).
Record eSIM capability (true/false) in the Device Management System using the Device Record template (CSV format).
Record activation status in the Device Management System using the Device Record template (CSV format).
Record activation date in the Device Management System using the Device Record template (CSV format).
If a last eSIM transfer date exists, record it; otherwise leave the field blank in the Device Record template (CSV format).
must_not: Must not leave required fields (device ID, device type, model, activation status, activation date) empty.
Must not use values for device type outside the defined list (phone, tablet, router, watch, other).
notes: IMEI number is optional.
eSIM capability should be captured as a boolean (true/false).

procedures.name: Bill Management
procedures.applies_when: When a bill is to be created, issued, or its status updated.
steps: Create a bill record containing: bill ID, customer ID, billing period (start and end dates), issue date, total amount due, due date, line items (charges, fees, credits), and status.
must_not: Assign a status outside the defined types: Draft, Issued, Paid, Overdue, Awaiting Payment, Disputed.
notes: Use only the six bill status types defined in the SOP.

procedures.name: Customer Lookup
procedures.applies_when: An agent needs to retrieve a customer's information to process a request.

inputs.fact: Full name with date of birth

decisions.rule: If phone number is provided, use phone number; else if customer ID is provided, use customer ID; else if full name and date of birth are provided, use name lookup; else error.
decisions.then: Proceed with the selected lookup method.
decisions.else: Return an error indicating insufficient identification data.

decisions.rule: When using name lookup, date of birth must be present and match the record.
decisions.then: Allow access to customer record.
decisions.else: Reject lookup and request correct date of birth.

steps: Identify which identifier is available (phone number, customer ID, or full name with date of birth).
Query the Customer Database using the selected identifier.
If name lookup is used, apply decision 'dob_verification' to confirm the date of birth.
deadlines: Complete the lookup and present results within 2 minutes of the request.
must_not: Do not perform a name lookup without a date of birth.
Do not disclose customer information without successful verification.
notes: Use phone number as the primary identifier for fastest lookup.
If multiple identifiers are provided, prioritize in the order: phone number, customer ID, full name with DOB.

links.when: if the retrieved record shows an overdue bill
if the retrieved record indicates the line is suspended

procedures.name: Overdue Bill Payment
procedures.applies_when: When a user has an overdue bill and wants to make a payment.

decisions.then: send payment request
decisions.else: do not send request; inform user bill is not overdue

decisions.rule: no other bill in AWAITING PAYMENT status
decisions.then: proceed with payment request
decisions.else: cannot send request; inform user of existing pending payment request

decisions.then: inform user payment successful
decisions.else: do not inform; investigate payment failure

steps: Check the bill status to make sure it is overdue.
Check the bill amount due.
Verify that no other bill is in AWAITING PAYMENT status.
Send the user a payment request for the overdue bill (this will change the status of the bill to AWAITING PAYMENT).
Inform the user that a payment request has been sent and instruct them to check their payment requests using the check_payment_request tool.
If the user accepts the payment request, use the make_payment tool to make the payment.
After the payment is made, verify that the bill status is updated to PAID.
Inform the user that the bill has been paid.
must_not: Do not send a payment request if the bill is not overdue.
Do not allow more than one bill in AWAITING PAYMENT status at a time.
notes: Always verify the overdue status before sending a payment request.
Always confirm the bill status is PAID before informing the user of successful payment.

procedures.name: Line Suspension Management
procedures.applies_when: When a line is currently suspended and the agent needs to determine whether to lift the suspension.

decisions.then: Lift suspension

steps: Retrieve the overdue bill amount from the Billing System.
Retrieve the contract end date from the Customer Database.
If overdue bill amount is zero and contract end date is today or in the future, execute the lift‑suspension command in the Line Management System.
If the suspension is lifted, send a notification to the user instructing them to reboot their device to restore service.
must_not: Do not lift the suspension if the line's contract end date is in the past, even if all overdue bills have been paid.
notes: After the line is resumed, the user must reboot their device to regain service.

procedures.name: Data Refueling
procedures.applies_when: The user's data usage for a line exceeds the plan's data limit.

inputs.fact: Current data usage for the line
Phone number of the line to be refueled

decisions.rule: Current data usage > Plan's monthly data limit
decisions.then: Proceed to data refueling workflow
Approve refuel

steps: Ask the customer how much data they want to refuel (in GB).
Confirm the price (Requested GB × Price per GB) with the customer.
Apply the refueled data to the line associated with the phone number the user provided.
must_not: Refuel more than 2 GB in a single transaction.
notes: Prioritize quick confirmation of price to avoid further connectivity loss.

procedures.name: Change Plan
procedures.applies_when: When a user requests to change to a different plan for one of their lines.

inputs.fact: Line identifier (phone number or line ID) the user wants to change

decisions.rule: User confirms the calculated price of the new plan
decisions.then: Apply the selected plan to the identified line
decisions.else: Do not apply the plan and inform the user that the change is cancelled

steps: Identify the line the user wants to change the plan for (use the phone number or line ID provided).
Gather available plans from the plan catalog.
Ask the user to select one of the available plans.
Calculate the price of the new plan based on the selected option.
Confirm the price with the user.
Apply the plan to the line associated with the phone number the user provided.
must_not: Do not apply the new plan without the user confirming the price.
notes: Handle the request promptly to avoid service interruption.

procedures.name: Data Roaming
procedures.applies_when: When a user is traveling outside their home network.

decisions.then: user can use their phone's data connection in areas outside their home network
decisions.else: enable roaming for the line at no cost for the user

steps: Verify the user is traveling outside their home network.
Check if the line is roaming enabled.
If the line is not roaming enabled, enable it at no cost for the user.
Inform the user they can use their phone's data connection in areas outside their home network.

procedures.name: Diagnostic Procedure for Phone Connectivity Issues
procedures.applies_when: When a user reports issues with cellular service, mobile data, or MMS.

inputs.fact: Phone's connection status to cellular networks and Wi‑Fi
Data‑limiting features status (Data Saver, background data restriction)
Wi‑Fi connection status (on/off, SSID, signal strength)
Specific app details (permissions, background data usage)
MMS send capability of the messaging app

decisions.rule: if signal strength is "none" or "poor" (📵 No Signal or 📶¹ Poor)
decisions.then: recommend checking network coverage or moving to a better signal area

decisions.rule: if Data Saver is on (🔽 Data Saver) and background data is restricted globally
decisions.then: note that data‑saving may be limiting app traffic

decisions.rule: if mobile data status is disabled (📵 Data Disabled)
decisions.then: highlight that mobile data must be enabled for data‑related issues
flag MMS functionality as blocked

steps: run check_status_bar – retrieve status‑bar icons (Airplane Mode, signal strength, network technology, mobile data, Data Saver, Wi‑Fi, VPN, battery level)
run check_network_status – verify airplane mode, signal strength, network type, mobile data enabled, data roaming enabled
run check_network_mode_preference – read preferred cellular network type (5G/4G/3G/2G)
run check_sim_status – display SIM card state (active, missing, PIN/PUK locked)
run check_data_restriction_status – show Data Saver mode and global background data restriction
run check_apn_settings – list current APN name and MMSC URL for picture messaging
run check_wifi_status – indicate Wi‑Fi on/off, connected SSID, and signal strength
run check_wifi_calling_status – confirm Wi‑Fi Calling enabled/disabled
run check_vpn_status – display VPN connection state and details
run check_installed_apps – output names of all installed apps
run check_app_status for the default messaging app – show its permissions and background data usage
run check_app_permissions for the default messaging app – list granted permissions (storage, camera, location, etc.)
run run_speed_test – measure download speed and classify as unknown/very poor/poor/fair/good/excellent
run can_send_mms – verify if the messaging app can send MMS messages
deadlines: All steps must be completed within 5 minutes of initiation
Each individual check should return results within 30 seconds
must_not: must not modify any device settings (read‑only only)
must not restart the device
must not uninstall or install apps
notes: Prioritize check_status_bar as it provides a quick visual summary
If any decision flags a problem, link to the appropriate fix section before proceeding further

links.when: any decision indicates a configuration or hardware issue

procedures.name: Fix Actions (Write/Modify)
procedures.applies_when: When a diagnostic identifies a configuration or connectivity issue that requires changing device settings.
steps: set_network_mode_preference – Changes the type of cellular network your phone prefers to connect to (e.g., 5G, 4G, 3G).
toggle_airplane_mode – Turns Airplane Mode ON or OFF. When ON, it disconnects all wireless communications including cellular, Wi‑Fi, and Bluetooth.
reseat_sim_card – Simulates removing and reinserting your SIM card. This can help resolve recognition issues.
toggle_data – Turns your phone's mobile data connection ON or OFF. Controls whether your phone can use cellular data for internet access when Wi‑Fi is unavailable.
toggle_roaming – Turns Data Roaming ON or OFF. When ON, roaming is enabled and your phone can use data networks in areas outside your carrier's coverage.
toggle_data_saver_mode – Turns Data Saver mode ON or OFF. When ON, it reduces data usage, which may affect data speed.
set_apn_settings – Sets the APN settings for the phone.
reset_apn_settings – Resets your APN settings to the default settings.
toggle_wifi – Turns your phone's Wi‑Fi radio ON or OFF. Controls whether your phone can discover and connect to wireless networks for internet access.
toggle_wifi_calling – Turns Wi‑Fi Calling ON or OFF. This feature allows you to make and receive calls over Wi‑Fi instead of the cellular network, which can help in areas with weak cellular signal.
connect_vpn – Connects to your VPN (Virtual Private Network).
disconnect_vpn – Disconnects any active VPN (Virtual Private Network) connection. Stops routing your internet traffic through a VPN server, which might affect connection speed or access to content.
grant_app_permission – Gives a specific permission to an app (like access to storage, camera, or location). Required for some app functions to work properly.
reboot_device – Restarts your phone completely. This can help resolve many temporary software glitches by refreshing all running services and connections.
notes: Execute actions in the order that matches the identified issue; for example, toggle Airplane Mode before reseating the SIM if the SIM is not recognized.

procedures.name: SIM Card Issues
procedures.applies_when: When the user experiences loss of cellular service that may be caused by a problem with the SIM card.

decisions.then: Guide the user to reseat the SIM card using `reseat_sim_card()`.
Escalate to technical support for assistance with SIM security.
decisions.else: Inform the user that the SIM is likely okay (status "Active").

steps: Run `check_sim_status()` to obtain the current SIM card status.
If the status is "Missing", guide the user to use `reseat_sim_card()` to ensure the SIM card is correctly inserted.
If the status is "Locked", escalate to technical support for assistance with SIM security.
If the status is "Active", inform the user that the SIM itself is likely okay.

procedures.name: Incorrect APN Settings

decisions.then: Proceed with APN reset and device reboot

steps: Use `reset_apn_settings()` to reset the APN settings.
Use `reboot_device()` for the changes to apply.
must_not: Do not modify any other network settings before resetting APN.
notes: Access Point Name (APN) settings are crucial for network connectivity.
High priority: required for restoring connectivity.

procedures.name: Diagnosing Mobile Data Issues
procedures.applies_when: When a user reports that mobile data is unavailable, slow, or otherwise not performing as expected.

decisions.then: Classify issue as 'No Mobile Data Connection'
Classify issue as 'Slow Mobile Data'

steps: Execute `run_speed_test()` on the device to obtain the current mobile data status.
Capture the returned value (either 'no connection' or a speed rating such as 'Excellent', 'Good', 'Fair', etc.).
Apply decision d1: if the result is 'no connection', record the issue as a lack of mobile data connectivity.
If the result is not 'no connection', apply decision d2: compare the speed rating against the threshold 'Excellent'.
Record the classification ('Slow Mobile Data' or 'Mobile Data Functional') for further troubleshooting or reporting.
must_not: Do not modify any device settings or write/modify data during this diagnostic step.
notes: Prioritize the speed test as the first diagnostic action; it provides a clear, read‑only indication of connectivity status.
Any speed below 'Excellent' is considered slow per SOP guidance.

links.when: Issue classified as 'No Mobile Data Connection' or 'Slow Mobile Data'

procedures.name: Data Plan Limits Reached
procedures.applies_when: The user's data usage for the line associated with the provided phone number exceeds the plan's monthly data limit.

inputs.fact: User's data usage for the line exceeds the plan's data limit

decisions.rule: if data_usage > plan_monthly_limit then data connectivity will be lost
decisions.then: Notify user and present remediation options

steps: 1. Query the billing system for the line's monthly_data_used and compare it to the plan_monthly_limit.
2. If usage exceeds the limit, generate a notification to the user stating: "Data connectivity will be lost because your usage exceeds the plan's data limit."
3. Present the user with the two remediation options exactly as worded in the SOP:
a. "Change to a plan with more data."
b. "Add more data to the line by \"refueling\" data at a price per GB specified by the plan."
4. Include a reference to the general policy for guidelines on those options in the notification.
deadlines: All steps must be completed immediately after the usage exceeds the limit (within the same operational window).
must_not: Do not change the user's plan without explicit consent.
Do not provide additional data beyond the plan limit without the user selecting the "refueling" option.
notes: High priority: loss of connectivity impacts user experience.
Use the exact wording from the SOP for options and notifications.

procedures.name: Verifying APN (MMSC URL) for MMS
procedures.applies_when: The MMSC URL in the device's APN settings is not set.

inputs.fact: MMSC URL is missing or empty

decisions.then: reset_apn_settings()

steps: Run `check_apn_settings()` to inspect the current APN configuration and verify whether the MMSC URL is present.
If `check_apn_settings()` shows the MMSC URL is not set, guide the user to execute `reset_apn_settings()` to reset the APN settings to their defaults.
After the APN reset, instruct the user to run `reboot_device()` so the new settings take effect.
deadlines: All steps must be completed within the same support session.
must_not: Do not manually edit any other APN fields besides resetting the entire APN configuration.
Do not skip the device reboot after resetting APN settings.
notes: High priority: without a correct MMSC URL, MMS cannot be sent or received.

global_rules.rule: As a telecom agent, you can help users with technical support, overdue bill payment, line suspension, and plan options.
You should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments.

You should only make one tool call at a time, and if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously. If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time.
You should deny user requests that are against this policy.

You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. To transfer, first make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents, and then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user.
You should try your best to resolve the issue for the user before transferring the user to a human agent.
You must first identify the customer.
Make sure you try all the possible ways to resolve the user's issue before transferring to a human agent.

global_rules.src: Common Service Issues and Their Causes
global_rules.rule: Airplane Mode disables all wireless radios, including cellular.
If the line is suspended and the agent cannot lift the suspension, escalate to technical support.
Mobile data requires cellular service; if cellular service is absent, troubleshoot cellular first.
MMS requires both cellular service and mobile data; ensure both are functional before troubleshooting MMS.
If Data Saver mode is ON, it may restrict background data usage.
If VPN is ON and performance is Poor, disconnect the VPN.
If network mode preference is 2G or 3G, set it to 4g_5g_preferred for better service.

global_rules.src: Investigating Wi‑Fi Calling Interference with MMS
global_rules.rule: If Wi‑Fi Calling is ON, it may interfere with MMS; turn it OFF.
If the messaging app lacks storage or sms permissions, grant them.

triage.name: Technical Support Triage
steps: Identify the customer (stop when the customer is identified).

definitions.Airplane Mode: A device setting that disables all wireless radios, including cellular, Wi‑Fi, Bluetooth, and NFC.
definitions.SIM Card: A subscriber identity module that stores the user's carrier credentials; it must be properly inserted and unlocked for service.
definitions.APN: Access Point Name – the carrier‑specific settings that allow a device to connect to the mobile data network.
definitions.MMS: Multimedia Messaging Service, an extension of SMS that enables sending pictures, videos, and audio.
definitions.Mobile Data: The service that allows a phone to access the internet over the carrier's cellular network.
definitions.Data Saver Mode: A phone feature that restricts background data usage to conserve data allowance.
definitions.VPN: Virtual Private Network – encrypts internet traffic and can affect speed or connectivity when active.
definitions.Network Mode Preference: The setting that determines which cellular technologies (2G/3G/4G/5G) the phone may use.
definitions.Wi‑Fi Calling: A feature that routes voice calls over Wi‑Fi instead of the cellular network; it can interfere with MMS on some carriers.

escalation.name: Technical Support Escalation
steps: If the line is suspended and the agent cannot lift the suspension per policy, create an escalation ticket and assign to technical support.
If all troubleshooting steps (1‑10 in triage) have been exhausted without resolution, create an escalation ticket.
must_not: Do not transfer the user to a human agent before attempting all troubleshooting steps outlined in the triage section.
